cultural.vision_reason: The image shows adinkra-stamped cloth with woven kente strips, classic Ashanti/Akan textile construction and symbolism, matching the claimed ethnicity and category.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Cloth; made of hand-woven cotton; strips of multicoloured (one strip green, yellow and black, the other green,yellow, pink, black and blue) "kente" cloth alternating with white cloth (sewn together lengthwise) stamped with four alternating squares of black adinkra stamps: 1) concentric circles ("adinkrahene" the chief of the adinkra symbols, representing greatness, charisma or leadership); 2) square with cross inside with square in each corner ("nsaa" translated "a type of hand-woven cloth" representing excellence, genuineness and authenticity); 3) crescent on three black lines  ("akoben" translated "war horn" representing vigilance and wariness); 4) X with flower stamped over top.
